newsitem.title: USA: Natgas futures end mixed, then lose ground on AGAs.
newsitem.headline: Natgas futures end mixed, then lose ground on AGAs.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures, hit by a late wave of profit taking Wednesday, ended mixed in a fairly active session, then lost ground on ACCESS after an unexpectedly bearish weekly AGA stock report, sources said.

November ended 3.2 cents higher at $2.47 per million British thermal units after earlier rallying to $2.59, then tumbled to $2.37 on ACCESS after the report. December eased 0.1 cent to close at $2.604. Others finished mixed.
"Everyone was long and got toasted. This (AGAs) was an unexpected number and could set us up for more liquidation," said one East Coast trader.
AGA said Wednesday that U.S. gas stocks rose last week by 94 bcf. A Reuter poll earlier showed most expected a 70-75 bcf build.

While traders said the unexpected stock jump should put a temporary damper on the bulls, some expected forecasts for cool Midwest and East Coast weather through next week to keep the bears in control.
"Longer-term, the uptrend is still intact, but we may have gotten a little ahead of ourselves," a trader said.
Technically, traders pegged November support in the $2.30 area, with resistance at Wednesday's high of $2.59.

Cash sources said Gulf Coast prices jumped more than 10 cents Wednesday to about the $2.30 mark. Midcon pipes were up almost 15 cents to the high-teens. Gas at the New York city gate was pegged at about $2.60, also up more than a dime.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip fell one-half cent to $2.232. NYMEX said 58,566 Hub contracts traded, up from Tuesday's revised tally of 43,919.
NYMEX November Alberta natgas settled three cents higher at $1.115, while deferreds closed up by one-half to 6.5 cents. NYMEX said 176 Alberta contracts traded compared to Tuesday's total of 243.
NYMEX Permian natgas was untraded but November settled with a six-cent gain at $2.11. Deferreds ended up by one to three cents.

On the KCBT, November settled four cents higher at $2.19, while deferreds ended up by one to three cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 0.8 cent to 28.0 cents (NYMEX premium). --J Silha, New York Power Desk 212-859-1624
